data.title: The Standard Reserve Raises 583.6 ETH in Genesis Charters Mint
data.description:
The Standard Reserve said it has completed its Genesis Charters mint and raised 583.6 ETH. According to ChainCatcher, the mint price for whitelist participants was 0.15 ETH, while most public auction sales cleared between 1.23 ETH and 1.25 ETH.

The project said all proceeds will go entirely to initial liquidity and the protocol treasury, with no allocation to the team. STANDARD briefly reached a market capitalization of $18.38 million and was at $17.06 million at the time of reporting. The token used a temporary anti-sniping tax during its first hour of trading, starting at 90% and decaying exponentially, with most of the reduction occurring in the first five minutes before normal trading fees resumed after one hour.

data.title: Derive Community Proposes Deploying V3 and Phasing Out Derive Chain
data.description: The Derive community has released a proposal to deploy V3 and gradually shut down Derive Chain. According to Foresight News, the proposal includes launching Derive V3, migrating all V2 positions and balances to V3's genesis state, and moving cross-chain funds to L1 before phasing out Derive Chain.

data.title: India’s Auction Revamp Could Benefit Exchanges and Brokers
data.description: Stock exchanges and brokers could be among the biggest beneficiaries of the Securities and Exchange Board of India’s proposed changes to the newly launched closing auction system, according to Bloomberg. Market makers may face tighter constraints under the proposal.

data.title: Polymarket Chicago White Sox Option Jumps to 95.6% Amid Sharp Volatility
data.description: Catcher Predict reported sharp volatility in the Polymarket submarket for the Chicago White Sox vs. Cleveland Guardians event, with the Chicago White Sox option rising from 37.5% one hour earlier to 95.6% at the time of monitoring. According to ChainCatcher, the move reflected a 58.1% swing and may have been influenced by breaking news.

data.title: Mike Novogratz Says U.S. Could Lose Crypto Regulation If Clarity Act Stalls
data.description: Mike Novogratz said on X that if the Clarity Act does not advance tomorrow, the U.S. could be unable to secure crypto regulation for a long time, or even permanently. According to Odaily, he said this would hurt the U.S. and push more of the industry overseas, adding that the digital and blockchain revolution will continue and urging bipartisan senators to focus on the bigger picture.

data.title: a16z Partner Josh Elman Says Product Management Is Storytelling
data.description:
a16z partner Josh Elman said product management is about storytelling, recalling that he began his career as an engineer at RealNetworks and worked on the product and engineering teams for RealPlayer, which had hundreds of millions of users. According to ChainCatcher, he said he was later interviewed by Reid Hoffman for LinkedIn and was asked what a product manager’s output is; he first answered a specification document, but later said that was the wrong answer and that the real output is a story people can pass along without him present.

Elman said he once wrote a 120-page specification document at LinkedIn. He added that AI has collapsed the cost of making products and reversed the development loop, shifting the process from specifications and scope to building and experience. He said teams should use AI to quickly build prototypes, see how they feel, and then design and release after the prototype proves better than assumptions.

He also said demos are now nearly free while working products are not, making decisions about what to build a debate over influence. Elman said vision consists of purpose, core actions, and cycles, and that teams should ask whether people are truly using the product. He added that guiding users is the most important moment in storytelling.

data.title: TSMC 3nm and 2nm Capacity Remains Tight as NVIDIA, Apple, AWS, and MediaTek Compete for Supply
data.description:
TSMC’s 3nm and 2nm advanced process capacity, along with CoWoS advanced packaging, remains in short supply as demand stays strong in late Q3 2026. According to ChainCatcher, NVIDIA and Apple continue to absorb much of the advanced process and packaging supply, while Amazon Web Services’ Annapurna has recently increased AI chip tape-outs and secured more 3nm capacity.

MediaTek is also competing for 2nm and 3nm capacity and CoWoS-S/L supply, driven by large orders tied to Google TPU-related chips. Market reports said TSMC has recently adjusted its capacity allocation, and MediaTek’s 3nm and 2nm scheduling has been fine-tuned after winning the Google TPU order. The next-generation TPU v9 is expected to use both TSMC CoWoS-L and Intel EMIB-T. TSMC’s main 3nm customer is now NVIDIA, which surpassed Apple as the largest customer in 2025, while 2nm demand is led by Apple and others.

TSMC has accelerated expansion since early 2026. By the end of October, 2nm monthly capacity at Hsinchu Baoshan Fab 20 and Kaohsiung Fab 22 is expected to reach 50,000 wafers each, or about 100,000 wafers combined, while 3nm monthly capacity in Tainan is expected to reach about 185,000 wafers. Overall utilization was about 96.2% at the end of September, with processes from 16nm and 12nm down to 2nm running at 100%. Packaging shortages have also pushed advanced packaging orders outward, with ASE Group’s SPIL taking priority, followed by Amkor and Powertech. Powertech’s related testing and packaging capacity is fully booked, with order visibility extending to 2028.

data.title: AI Pullback Reflects Guardrail Debate, Says Manulife's Marc Franklin
data.description:
Manulife Investment Management Head of Multi-Asset Solutions Marc Franklin said the recent pullback in AI stocks reflects debate over regulatory guardrails and the pace of development, not structural damage to growth, according to Bloomberg.

He said shifting regulatory frameworks and open-source quantum tools will add competitive pressure on high-margin technology suppliers.

data.title: Google Considers New Data Center Project in New Mexico's Lea County
data.description: Google said it is considering building a new data center project in Lea County, New Mexico, and that discussions are still ongoing with many details yet to be finalized, according to Jiemian News. The company did not disclose a timeline, investment size or other project specifics.

data.title: Anthropic Reportedly Picks Nasdaq for IPO as Musk Says SpaceX May Launch Nvidia AI Computer Into Space Next Year
data.description:
Anthropic PBC has reportedly chosen Nasdaq as its listing venue and is seeking to raise as much as or more than SpaceX in an IPO that could come as early as October, according to Jiemian News. Separately, Elon Musk said on social media on September 13 that he was “extremely confident” SpaceX will send Nvidia’s VR NLV72 AI computer into space next year.

Jiemian News also reported that Anthropic, OpenAI and Google have been discussing cooperation to create an AI industry standards body, with working-group meetings still under way. In a separate financing update, SoftBank Group said it secured a $11.87 billion loan to support its investment in OpenAI, above its earlier $10 billion target, after finalizing a two-year loan agreement last week with commitments from about 20 banks.

On September 14, Alibaba Cloud said DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has been launched on the Qwen AI platform, with related API services and a Token Plan now available. Also on September 14, ByteDance's Doubao Phone Assistant consumer version was officially released, with its first handset, the Nubia NaviX Ultra, set to go on sale on September 16.

data.title: Senate Democrats Prepare Counterproposal to Revised CLARITY Act Text
data.description: Senate Democrats working on the crypto market structure bill are reportedly preparing a counterproposal to Republicans’ latest revised CLARITY Act text, even after GOP lawmakers described it as their “last, best and final offer” when they released it Sunday. According to Cointelegraph, Democrats working on the bill met in Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s office on Monday, and some lawmakers remain dissatisfied with the crypto ethics language in the latest version of the text. Senator Mark Warner said, “The Democrats who’ve been working on this in good faith are sending a counterproposal,” as he exited the meeting. The move comes ahead of a crucial Senate procedural vote on Tuesday, which will determine whether the Senate can advance the bill toward floor consideration.

data.title: Dragonfly Partner Haseeb Qureshi Says Robinhood Chain Fee Cuts Reduced Revenue but Kept DEX Volume Strong
data.description:
Dragonfly partner Haseeb Qureshi said Robinhood’s decision to raise Robinhood Chain’s gas limit and lower user fees sharply reduced on-chain revenue, while DEX trading volume remained strong and was second only to Solana.

According to Odaily, Qureshi said the move was intentional rather than a mistake. He said Robinhood appears to value expanding on-chain capacity, bringing more tokenized assets onchain, and increasing blockchain economic activity over maximizing short-term ordering revenue. He added that achieving those goals requires larger network capacity and lower transaction fees.

data.title: Tom Lee Agrees With Mark Zandi That the Fed Can Wait on Policy Decisions
data.description: Tom Lee said on X that he agrees with Mark Zandi’s view that the Federal Reserve does not need to choose immediately between two options and can wait. According to Odaily, Goldman Sachs expects the supply shock pushing core PCE higher to be 1.75 percentage points now and to ease by 100 basis points to 0.75 percentage points by early 2027. Lee also said markets may rise after an event when investors have already prepared for negative news.

data.title: Jack Dorsey Supports Open AI Model Releases and Independent Safety Reviews
data.description:
Jack Dorsey said he supports open AI model releases, independent evaluations, and reviews of dangerous capabilities. According to Odaily, he argued that open-weight models allow independent researchers to reproduce results, identify problems, and develop safeguards.

He opposed industry-wide limits on compute, training runs, and model development negotiated by leading labs, saying such restrictions could leave current leaders as the only participants and exclude groups that can find problems or build alternatives. Dorsey said restricting general-purpose model releases should be a last resort, used only when independently reviewable evidence shows that release would significantly increase catastrophic risks that narrower measures cannot address. He also said he wants users to be able to run and control AI tools on their own devices.

data.title: Cambria Foundation Launches to Oversee Protocol Development and Native Token RSGP
data.description:
Cambria Foundation has been established to manage and advance the Cambria protocol, community, and ecosystem. According to ChainCatcher, the foundation said it will introduce a native token, RSGP, to serve as the core of the ecosystem’s consensus mechanism and support the upcoming permanent game world Genesis and other roadmap plans.

Genesis is expected to include persistent assets, guild treasuries, resource competition, and high-risk war gameplay, with incentives guided by the protocol and RSGP holders. Eligible historical Cambria users may opt into the Genesis event selection protocol, with eligibility closing at 11:00 PM Eastern Time on September 29, 2026. More information about RSGP will be released before the Genesis event.

data.title: AI Researcher Calls for Indefinite Halt to Frontier AI Development
data.description:
Canadian AI researcher David Krueger said only slowing AI development would not be enough to avoid a doomsday scenario. According to Sina Finance, Krueger called for an immediate, indefinite pause in frontier AI research and development.

Krueger, an assistant professor of AI at the University of Montreal and a core academic member of Quebec AI institute Mila, said the current testing methods for AI are no longer reliable. He said the tests have essentially failed because AI can disguise itself and deceive them.

He made the remarks after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on AI companies to slow their pace of development. The proposal was supported by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.

Krueger said he believes the measures proposed by Amodei are not strong enough and are moving too slowly. He also said that if AI systems go out of control, they could replicate across many computers, making it difficult to know which devices to shut down.

On Monday, Canadian federal AI minister Evan Solomon said AI will be regulated to protect Canadians. He also said he spoke with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman on Sunday morning and will announce an AI safety measure with Canadian computer scientist Yoshua Bengio on Wednesday.

data.title: Castle Labs Says Over $38 Billion in Assets Have Been Tokenized On-Chain
data.description:
Research firm Castle Labs said more than $38 billion in assets have now been tokenized on-chain. According to ChainCatcher, U.S. Treasuries account for over $15.9 billion, followed by commodities at $4.9 billion, active strategies at $3.6 billion, asset-backed credit at $2.56 billion, and equities at $2.52 billion.

Castle Labs cited Mantle, an Ethereum layer-2 network, as an example of current real-world asset adoption. According to ChainCatcher, the Mantle ecosystem currently holds more than $225 million in assets, with over 60% in the active RWA strategy Mantle Index Four Fund, 21% in syrupUSDT, 15% in Ondo USDY, and 2% in xStocks. The firm said 96% of RWA value is concentrated in yield-bearing assets, and xStocks has grown to more than $4.4 million since launching in March.

Castle Labs said listed assets are now relatively easy to bring on-chain, but the harder task is turning them into effective capital after tokenization. It said tokenized assets must be tradable in deep liquidity, usable as collateral, composable across venues, and broadly usable, or they may worsen liquidity fragmentation. The firm added that wider RWA adoption will require offering utility beyond traditional finance in accessibility and composability.
